title: Make a simple and advanced initsl setup wizards
body:
From the version we used for years with our G4, to what xDrip had evolved into, now that we have a G6. There are sooooo many options now, and the graph shows way lots more detail.

It would be nice to have a basic and advanced setup wizards.

I was showing xDrip with our G6 at a friends diabetes party tonight and they all loved xDrip, but were intimdated with the amount of data shown on the home screen. They just want it to look simple and clean, kind of like the Dexcom app.

And while you can adjust the display settings to show very little, you have to really mess with the settings to do so.

Because of this, I suggest adding a wizard that prompts you on the first setup for a clean and simple setup with minimal options and display settings enabled, and then an advanced choice that enables all but experimental options.

This way, people who are new to xDrip can go the simple and clean route first, who may not be as tech savvy. And still get the benefits of this amazing app.

Thanks for your consideration.

comments.body: As far as I know it already does some of this, did you start with a fresh installation? The first page should be the setup wizard asking for data source selection and many of the menu items are hidden until you first receive data.

It does to a degree. Just having upgraded from a very old version of xDrip recently, I was overwhelmed with the newer options, which is great by the way. But even though many are off. I still had to go through all the menus to find the options I was used to. And then to try and explain what's needed for a new user, it can be overwhelming for them to.

If anything, perhaps some guides by users like me would help. As each setup and rig is unique and requires different settings for best use.

I write help guides for my job, perhaps I can assist here?

i kinda have to disagree with the original poster. i found xdrip extremely simple to setup for my blucon and miaomiao. i had to change no settings at all....

there is already a wiki help page with a tutorial on blucon and wear setup.
